intro: Raasta finds the most scenic walk in Philadelphia, not the fastest one. Tell it your mood and how many extra minutes you can spare, and it builds a real route, then narrates it as you go.

A Python engine scores all 196,411 walkable street segments for trees, parks, water, public art and history. A language model turns your mood into weights, but it never picks the streets, and nothing can switch off what is dangerous.

title: Learning to Ski from NYC and Philly
kicker: Every ski area within three hours of New York or Philadelphia, ranked by beginner terrain and set on its real mountain.

tools.name: Python
tools.use: one notebook builds the whole page, with NumPy, SciPy and GeoPandas

tools.use: trail lengths in UTM, the ranked list, the trail and lift layers

tools.name: ArcGIS Pro
tools.use: 3 m USGS elevation per mountain, a multidirectional hillshade and 20 m contours, through arcpy

tools.name: MapLibre GL JS
tools.use: the page, which builds its own 3D terrain tiles in the browser

tools.name: Mapbox Matrix API
tools.use: drive times from each city, no traffic

tools.name: mapkit
tools.use: the shared toolkit: credits, style, the publish step

intro: Learning to ski from New York or Philadelphia means a day trip, so this map starts with a rule: every ski area within three hours' drive of either city, with no traffic. It ranks them by beginner terrain, the kilometres of bunny hill and green trail, and puts each one on its real mountain.

The overview is a relief of the whole region from USGS elevation. Click a mountain and its own terrain loads: 3 m elevation, a multidirectional hillshade and 20 m contours made in ArcGIS Pro, on 3D tiles the page builds in the browser. Hover a trail for its length, drop and slope, with a profile that draws every trail on the mountain at one scale, so they compare. Trails and lifts come from OpenStreetMap through OpenSkiMap.

gallery.caption: Windham, selected. 3 m terrain, 20 m contours and every trail, with a profile of the longest green run.

gallery.alt: Blue Mountain in 3D, seen low over its base: the bunny hill outlined in orange with the magic carpets drawn black beside it, the green trails dotted up the slope, Blue Mountain highlighted at number 6 in the ranked list and its stats on the right.
gallery.caption: Blue Mountain, selected: a kilometre of bunny hill and nine magic carpets at the base, the green trails dotted up the slope.

source.notes: The opener (ski-hero.mp4: the overview, then Jiminy Peak with its trails highlighted in turn) and the lead clip beside the text (ski-snippet-2.mp4: Blue Mountain) are Gautami's own captures from Some Material/Ski, compressed by tools/prepare_media.py with first-frame posters; the card is the hero's map column at 14 s. The Windham still and the work tiles were captured from the live page with Playwright (tools/record_ski.py); the second still is a frame of ski-snippet-2.mp4 at 2 s (Blue Mountain), so the pair shows two resorts. The opener takes opener_fit top on a white opener_bg: the frame fills the screen under the header, anchored to its top edge so the map's own title is never cut (only the bottom is cropped), and on phones it is anchored to the top-left so the title column stays whole. opener_title false: the footage carries its own title, so no number, title, kicker or meta fade in over it. Coordinates are Jiminy Peak. Place and year as asked: New York + Philadelphia day trips · 2026.

title: Forested University
kicker: A university campus set inside a forest, from the aerial down to the atrium.
intro: A university campus set inside a forest. Seen from above, white buildings stand among the trees beside the water, with pink blossom along the paths that thread between them. One student housing block is pulled apart floor by floor, so the pines can be seen rising through every level.
At eye level the walkthroughs move through an atrium built around the trunks and along a street of brick blocks in winter. The visuals were built in Rhino and developed with AI image tools.

data: IM3 Open Source Data Center Atlas (PNNL), derived from OpenStreetMap
intro: Two interactive maps of the physical side of AI. Where AI Gets Built puts 1,472 existing US data centers on one map with the 34 new AI campuses already running and the 43 more that are coming. What AI Drinks lays the same campuses over the basins where water is already scarce: 39% of the new campuses sit in them.

Both are built in Python from the IM3 Data Center Atlas, Epoch AI's Frontier Data Centers list and WRI Aqueduct 4.0, and published as Mapbox GL pages with a floating card, hover details on every point and a legend that switches each layer on and off.
They are the first two studies in a series that follows the data centers into the water, power and climate risk around them. What AI Burns and Where AI Is at Risk come next.

intro: Five static maps from the first week of the 30 Day Map Challenge, each one a question about a place answered with a number or a line. The Big Sur Marathon is drawn in plan and section with three line weights and one red line, the 510 ft climb to Hurricane Point. San Francisco's blocks are coloured by what the city lets you build: outside parks and public land, half of it is zoned for one or two family houses.

In Philadelphia, 12 towers now rise above William Penn's hat, all of them behind his back, and together they block 18% of his horizon. In the city's most heat-vulnerable tracts, 98% of streets are a ten minute walk from a park, but only 32% reach one of ten acres. Bombay's 1843 map of the seven islands carries today's shoreline in red.

Every map starts from the same Python toolkit, mapkit: the palettes, the credits and the title card live in one style file, each map is a notebook run top to bottom, and a publish step turns it into a live page and a thumbnail.

system.note: One style file holds the palettes, the credits and the title card. Every map starts from the same template notebook, and a publish step turns a finished notebook into a live page, a thumbnail and a caption stub, so a new map is one run away.
typefaces: Fraunces for titles and Inter for everything else, by default.
A case of display faces kept in the kit for a map that asks for one: Cinzel, DM Serif Display, IM Fell English, Abril Fatface, Bebas Neue, Zilla Slab.
